svg.title: Access credential security tiers
svg.desc: A four-rung security ladder for access control credentials. Tier 4 at the top: MIFARE DESFire EV3, HID iCLASS Seos and LEGIC advant with AES-128 mutual authentication and no public crack — the 2026 baseline. Tier 3: MIFARE Plus SE and EV2, AES-128 with Classic emulation for staged migration. Tier 2: MIFARE Classic 1K and 4K, whose Crypto-1 cipher was broken in 2008 — replace at refresh. Tier 1 at the bottom: 125 kHz LF silicon with no cryptography, cloneable in under a minute — legacy maintenance only. Red marks the rungs with genuine security risk.
svg.text: The security ladder, top to bottom
Price the attack, not just the card — every rung below is still installed somewhere in 2026.
Tier 4 — MIFARE DESFire EV3 · HID iCLASS Seos · LEGIC advant
AES-128 mutual authentication, file-based applications, Random UID — no public crack as of 2026
Tier 3 — MIFARE Plus SE / EV2 (SL3 mode)
AES-128 with backwards-compatible Classic emulation — the stepping-stone for estates mid-migration
Crypto-1 stream cipher academically broken in 2008 — sector keys fall in minutes; replace at refresh
Tier 1 — 125 kHz LF (EM4100 · HID Prox · Indala)
No cryptography at all — cloneable in under a minute with commodity tools; legacy maintenance only
The rungs are drawn the same height; the attacks against them are not. Match the tier to the door, not to the budget line.
